chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said:

My mother had made a vow upon herself; she vowed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding one of her children, concerning something she feared for him, that she would fast the day that came upon her for as long as she lived. So she traveled with us to Mecca, and it became confusing for us regarding her fasting during the journey, so she did not know whether to fast or break her fast. So I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about that, and he said: 'She should not fast during the journey, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has removed His right from her during the journey, and she should fast what she made upon herself.' So I said to him, 'So what is that when she returns, if she leaves that (fasting)?' He said: 'No, I fear that she will see in her child, regarding whom she vowed, some of what she dislikes.'
ai.seo_question: How does a traveler fulfill a vow to fast if they are unsure whether to fast or break fast during the journey?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle that travel exemptions (rukhas) apply to the obligatory aspect of a vow, allowing the vow-maker to break the fast during travel without penalty. Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) further clarifies that the vow is not extinguished by the travel exemption; rather, the obligation to fast resumes upon her return to ensure the specific condition of her vow is fully met. This ruling highlights the distinction between the temporary suspension of duty due to hardship and the permanent fulfillment of the vowed commitment.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboun, from Ali Bin Raib, from Zurara who said,

‘My mother had made vow upon herself. She vowed for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic regarding one of her children with regards to something which she had feared over him, that she would be Fasting on that day which had come upon her, for as long as she lived. So she went out with use to Makkah. So that was confusing upon us, for her to be Fasting during the journey. So she did not know when she should be Fasting or breaking it. So I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She should not Fast during the journey. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Placed (dropped) it from her, being her right in the journey, and she should be Fasting what she had made it to be upon herself’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So what would be that when the day comes and she leaves that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No! I<sup>asws</sup> fear that she would see in her child that which she had vowed regarding it, some of what she had left’.
en.sarwar: 24. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “

My mother had made a vow and commitment. She had made a commitment for Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, about one of her children because of fear of something for him. She said that from that day on, she will fast all the time as long as she lives. She came out with us to Makkah, her fasting on the journey made us face questions, and she did not know if she must fast or not. I asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it and he (the Imam) said, ‘She must not fast on a journey. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has exempted her from His right during a journey; but she must fast otherwise for what she has committed herself to.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if she ignores her commitment? He (the Imam) said, ‘No, I fear that she may experience in her child that which made her to form such commitment.’”
